title.en: Fitting the Conversation: Token Budgets & Context Windows

description.en: Every LLM has a context limit, and long chats blow past it. The fix is a token budget: keep the most recent messages that fit and drop the rest. Build the trimmer every chatbot needs.

story_variants.en:
## The Wall Every Chatbot Hits

"A model's **context window** is finite — even 2026's big ones," Vaathiyaar says. "Let a conversation grow and eventually the whole history won't fit. Send it anyway and you get an error, or worse, a silently truncated prompt. So every real chat app runs a **token budget**: before each call, it trims the history to what fits — keeping the *most recent* messages, because those matter most."

### Newest First

Recency wins. The system keeps the latest messages and drops the oldest until the total fits the budget. (Production apps often *summarize* the dropped history, but the core move is this fit-to-budget trim.)

```
messages (oldest -> newest), each with a token count:
  [("m1", 40), ("m2", 30), ("m3", 25), ("m4", 20)]
budget = 60 tokens

walk from the NEWEST backwards, adding while it fits:
  m4 (20) -> total 20  keep
  m3 (25) -> total 45  keep
  m2 (30) -> total 75  STOP (over 60)
kept, in original order: [m3, m4]
```

### Why This Is Non-Negotiable

Skip budgeting and your app breaks the moment a chat gets long — which is exactly when users are most invested. It's a tiny function that prevents your most embarrassing failure mode.

> **Vaathiyaar's rule:** never send an unbounded history to an LLM. Budget every call. The newest tokens are the ones the model needs most.

Today you implement `fit_budget(messages, budget)` — keep the newest messages that fit, returned in original order.

explanation.en: Start from the newest message and move backwards
Stop as soon as the next message would overflow the window
It fits — keep it and add its cost to the running total
We collected newest-first; flip back to original chat order

instruction.en: Implement `fit_budget(messages, budget)`. `messages` is a list of `(text, token_cost)` tuples in chat order (oldest first). Keep the **newest** messages whose costs sum to at most `budget`, and return their **texts in original order**. Then print `fit_budget([("m1", 40), ("m2", 30), ("m3", 25), ("m4", 20)], 60)` (expected: `['m3', 'm4']`).

The oldest messages, since they set up the chat
The shortest messages, so that more of them fit
The newest messages, since they matter most

q.en: Spot the mistake: a trimmer loops `for text, cost in messages:` and adds messages while they fit. What goes wrong?
q.ta: தவறைக் கண்டுபிடி: ஒரு trimmer `for text, cost in messages:` என்று சுற்றி, பொருந்தும் வரை செய்திகளைச் சேர்க்கிறது. என்ன தவறு நடக்கிறது?

en: It returns the kept texts in reverse order
It keeps the oldest messages instead of the newest
Its total can go over the budget
It crashes because tuples can't be unpacked in a loop
ta: வைத்த texts-ஐ தலைகீழ் வரிசையில் திருப்பித் தரும்
புதிய செய்திகளுக்குப் பதிலாக பழைய செய்திகளை வைத்திருக்கும்
loop-இல் tuple-களைப் பிரிக்க முடியாததால் அது crash ஆகும்

q.en: A trimmer collects texts newest-first but forgets list(reversed(kept)). What does it return for the lesson's example (budget 60)?
q.ta: ஒரு trimmer புதியதிலிருந்து தொடங்கி texts-ஐச் சேகரிக்கிறது, ஆனால் list(reversed(kept)) செய்ய மறந்துவிடுகிறது. பாடத்தின் உதாரணத்துக்கு (budget 60) அது என்ன திருப்பித் தரும்?

uth_example:
def tokens(text):
    return len(text.split()) + 1

system = "You are a cooking assistant"
history = [
    "user: how long to boil eggs",
    "bot: about 9 minutes for hard boiled eggs",
    "user: and soft boiled",
    "bot: around 6 minutes then cool in water",
    "user: can I use the same pot for rice",
]
window = 30
budget = window - tokens(system)              # the system prompt is always sent

kept, used = [], 0
for msg in reversed(history):                 # newest first
    cost = tokens(msg)
    if used + cost > budget:
        break
    kept.insert(0, msg)
    used += cost

print(f"kept {len(kept)} of {len(history)} messages, {used + tokens(system)}/{window} tokens")
print(kept)
